The research object is an 8-stage axial flow compressor.
The compressor inlet conditions are standard atmospheric pressure (101,325 Pa) and temperature (288°C).
The original compressor backpressure is 600,000 Pa.
The CGNS (CFD General Notation System) standard format is used to extract the 3D numerical simulation data.
The S2 flow path design parameters and 3D simulation results are compared at the inlet and outlet of each compressor stage.
After iterative design optimization, the design adiabatic efficiency increased by 0.5% and the surge margin increased by over 5%.
The relative Mach number at the blade tip of the first stage rotor was found to be supersonic, indicating a need for more accurate subsonic aerodynamic design.
The first and last stages of the compressor were identified as needing the most improvement.
The CGNS data extraction method allows for more complete and accurate extraction of 3D simulation data compared to other techniques.
The iterative process of comparing S2 design and 3D simulation results, and then modifying the blade design accordingly, is an important procedure for improving axial flow compressor performance.
The authors developed a program to automate the extraction of CGNS format data for multi-stage axial compressors.
Central difference format is used for spatial discretization in the 3D numerical simulations.
The 3D simulations use the S-A turbulence model and a fourth-order Runge-Kutta method for time integration.
There are 61 stations for the S2 flow path design, 17 for radial clearance, and 49 for stationary blades.
The 3D numerical simulations are performed using the NUMECA Fine Turbo software.
